headline: S&P 500 settled at a prior cash close of 7,572 as cooler CPI and PPI data lifted megacap tech while chip stocks stumbled and US-Iran strikes kept oil above $80.
stance: Cautiously constructive, but the day is binary. Two back-to-back softer inflation prints (June CPI 3.5%, June PPI -0.3%) have trimmed rate-hike odds, and credit markets remain calm — all constructive. Against that, TSMC reports at 2 pm ET today: its guidance will either validate or deflate the AI chip trade that is holding the Nasdaq together. Overnight Asia saw semiconductor stocks tumble broadly, so the open is fragile until TSMC speaks.

news.head: Inflation cools two ways
news.body: June CPI came in at 3.5% year-over-year (below the 3.8% consensus) and June PPI fell 0.3% month-over-month (consensus was flat) — two consecutive data points pointing in the same direction.

news.head: Fed: no hike signal yet, but watch September
news.body: Fed Chair Warsh reiterated the Fed has 'no tolerance' for persistently elevated inflation but stopped short of a hawkish signal; markets still price roughly a 50% chance of a September rate hike.

news.head: US strikes on Iran continue
news.body: US Central Command launched additional strikes on Iran designed to degrade military capabilities used to target shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping oil elevated and inflation risk on the table.

news.head: Megacap tech led, chips fell
news.body: Apple hit an all-time high (+4%), Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft each gained ~3%, while Micron fell 8% and AMD, SanDisk, and Lam Research each dropped more than 3-5%.

news.head: BlackRock Q2 beat strongly
news.body: BlackRock reported $13.91 EPS vs $12.69 consensus on $7.08B revenue, sending shares up more than 7% Wednesday — its best day in over a year.

news.head: Asia chips tumbled overnight
news.body: Semiconductor stocks tumbled across Asia overnight, with South Korea's Kospi slumping as much as 7.3% and SK Hynix and Samsung leading losses, dragging regional equity markets lower.

news.head: TSMC reports today (2pm ET)
news.body: TSMC holds its Q2 2026 earnings call today at 2pm ET; consensus expects ~32% revenue growth year-over-year and 55%+ EPS growth, with the 3nm node sold out and 2nm ramping — guidance for Q3 and capex will be the key read-throughs for the entire AI chip chain.

news.head: Retail Sales & Jobless Claims at 8:30am
news.body: US June Retail Sales and weekly Initial Jobless Claims both print at 8:30am ET this morning — key reads on the consumer and labor market before the open.

implications: Softer CPI and PPI reduce — but do not eliminate — the risk of a September Fed rate hike; the 10-year yield (prior cash close 4.55%) may find a near-term ceiling if today's data also comes in benign.
US-Iran strikes are keeping WTI (prior cash close $80.24/bbl) elevated well above where it was when June CPI was measured; if oil holds here, the inflation relief may be partly reversed in July data.
Asia's overnight chip rout is a pre-market headwind for Nasdaq; TSMC's 2pm ET call is effectively the circuit-breaker — strong guidance could flip the session, weak guidance could accelerate selling.

The Japanese yen (prior cash close ¥162.11/$) sits at its weakest level in roughly 40 years (99th percentile of the past three years) — a structural stress point: any Bank of Japan policy surprise could send volatility rippling through global carry trades.

Positioning: In futures, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 (2nd percentile, 3-year low) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. In copper, speculators are heavily extended long (94th percentile) — a contrarian warning given copper's already extreme price (98th percentile of 3 years). In FX, the British pound carries an extended short (2nd percentile) despite its cash price sitting at a 3-year extreme high — creating meaningful squeeze risk. For 3M SOFR, speculators are at a 3-year short extreme (2nd percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean for rates.

watch.head: TSMC Q2 at 2pm ET
watch.body: Revenue vs the $39-40.2B guidance range, gross margin vs the guided 65.5-67.5%, and Q3 outlook are the three numbers that will determine whether the AI chip rally lives for another quarter.

watch.head: Retail Sales 8:30am ET
watch.body: June Retail Sales give the market an early read on whether the consumer is still spending; a soft number combined with the two soft inflation prints would sharply reduce September hike odds.

watch.head: WTI $80 level
watch.body: Crude holding above the prior cash close of $80.24 is a continuous drip of inflation risk — watch for any escalation or de-escalation headline out of the Strait of Hormuz.

watch.head: USD/JPY at ¥162
watch.body: The yen at a near-40-year low (99th percentile of 3 years) is the market's biggest structural landmine — any intervention signal from Japan's Ministry of Finance would spike volatility across carry-funded trades globally.

watch.head: Netflix after the close
watch.body: Netflix reports after the bell tonight with revenue expected at ~$12.6B (+13.5% YoY); subscriber trends and the ad-supported tier's growth will set the tone for media stocks into the weekend.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.55% — pulled back from a recent two-month high of 4.62% after two softer-than-expected inflation prints (CPI 3.5%, PPI -0.3% in June).
2-year Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.13% — the short end is most sensitive to Fed policy; markets price roughly a 50% chance of a September hike, down from ~70% earlier this week.
The yield curve (2s-10s) is a positive 42 basis points — no longer inverted, consistent with a slow-growth but not recessionary backdrop.
Real rates sit at 2.32% (10-year inflation-adjusted yield) — still meaningfully restrictive; the 10-year breakeven inflation expectation is 2.23%, well-anchored for now.
Term premium (the extra yield investors demand for holding long bonds) is 77.9 basis points — elevated, reflecting fiscal supply concerns and uncertainty about the Fed path.
Financial conditions remain loose by historical standards: the Chicago Fed's National Financial Conditions Index reads -0.535 (negative = easier than average), supporting risk assets.
US dollar (DXY): prior cash close 100.5 — softer inflation data has cooled the dollar's recent advance.
Bank credit growth running at 5.93% year-over-year; commercial paper spreads are only 18 basis points above overnight rates — no stress in short-term funding markets.
sections.positioning: In 3M SOFR futures, speculators have almost no bullish bets left — sitting at the 2nd percentile of the past three years, a contrarian floor suggesting the bond market may be pricing too much rate-hike risk. Speculators and commercial hedgers are at opposite extremes, reinforcing the contrarian lean.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: prior cash close 7,572.40 — up 0.38% Wednesday, a second consecutive gain driven by megacap tech rotation.
Nasdaq Composite: prior cash close 26,269.23 — up 0.62% Wednesday led by Apple (+4%), Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft (each ~3%), all hitting multi-week highs.
Dow Jones: prior cash close 52,658.64 — up 150 points Wednesday, quieter than the tech-heavy indexes.
VIX (fear gauge): prior cash close 15.67 — low, signaling the options market is not pricing much near-term risk, but the overnight Asia chip rout may push it higher at the open.
SKEW index at 148.5 — elevated, meaning the options market is quietly paying up for tail-risk protection even as headline volatility is low; a divergence worth noting.
Breadth is moderate: 61.6% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, and 65.7% above their 200-day — healthy but not euphoric.
Cyclicals check: ISM Manufacturing 53.3 and ISM Services 54.5 (both above 50, meaning expansion) provide fundamental support for the equity rally.

Valuation is stretched: the Shiller CAPE ratio stands at 42.18 — well above long-run averages — while the equity risk premium (extra return stocks offer over bonds) is -2.05%, meaning bonds are now more attractively valued than stocks on a risk-adjusted basis.
Asia sold off overnight led by chip stocks (Kospi -7.3% at worst); this is a direct pre-market headwind for US semiconductor names pending TSMC's 2pm ET results.
Alibaba US-listed shares rose ~5% in prior-session premarket on news that Alibaba's Qwen AI model will be integrated into Apple Intelligence in China.
sections.positioning: In Russell 2000 futures, speculators have almost no bullish bets left (2nd percentile of 3 years, a 3-year low) — historically a contrarian floor for small-cap stocks. Shorts are heavy relative to history, creating meaningful squeeze risk if today's macro data surprises to the upside.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — the world's largest contract chipmaker reports Q2 at 2pm ET today; large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options buying are both active on the signal, company insiders have been buying, and the stock is trading above its 200-day line. TSMC's guidance is the single most important read-through for the entire AI semiconductor investment thesis this earnings season.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs. investment-grade credit spread: 272 basis points (the extra yield junk bonds pay over safer corporate debt) — not signaling stress; credit markets are broadly calm.
Investment-grade option-adjusted spread: 79 basis points — tight, consistent with low default expectations in the corporate sector.
The equity-credit correlation is 0.698 — stocks and credit are moving closely together; if credit starts to widen, equities will likely follow.

Overnight repo (RRP) is nearly zero at $0.2 billion — meaning almost no cash is parked at the Fed overnight; bank reserves are ample at $3.1 trillion, and the Treasury General Account holds $774 billion, keeping system liquidity in good shape.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year — supportive of nominal asset prices but a mild inflationary undercurrent.

Copper at a prior cash close of $6.383/lb sits at the 98th percentile of the past three years (labeled extreme) — signaling the market is pricing strong global industrial demand, though speculators are heavily extended long (contrarian warning).
Wheat (prior cash close 677.75 c/bu) is also at an extreme 97.8th percentile — food commodity prices add to the tail-risk around inflation.
Loan syndication rates at 7.01% and bank credit at +5.93% YoY — lending conditions are tightening at the margin but not contracting.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (STNG) — energy tanker operator benefiting directly from elevated oil prices and Strait of Hormuz disruption; large off-exchange block buying and unusual options activity flagged on the scan.
